Job Description Summary 
Reporting to the Plant Leader this role will lead the Materials team to define and continuously improve material flow across an engineer-to-order Grid equipment factory operating in a Lean Manufacturing environment, spanning both in-house production and outsourced contract-manufacturer (CM) supply. The role owns inventory turns, working-capital landing, and material availability, and is accountable for the planning, procurement, material MRP setup, and analytics systems that drive them. 
The successful candidate combines outstanding cross-functional leadership with hands-on technical fluency in SAP, MRP, and work automation and analysis toolsets, and partners with Operations, Finance, and Sourcing to drive operations. 
 Job Description 
 Essential Responsibilities: 
 Drive a zero-tolerance environment for safety infractions.
 Lead weekly meetings and cross-functional planning sessions with engineering, production, contracts, and finance stakeholders; communicate priorities clearly across all organizational levels.
 Lead, develop, and motivate a team of buyers, planners and inventory control analysts, maintain performance management, objective setting and scorecards.
 Ensure materials/production planning, buying, and inventory control support sales, product development, customer service, and production cost-effectively.
 Plan, organize, direct and support, monitor and control the staff and functions related to planning materials, buying and inventory control.
 Continuously review and monitor departmental performance to ensure corporate objectives are being met. Review actions, risks, and shortages, and drive forecasting and material planning to protect the production schedule.
 Manage the end-to-end supply chain, including materials/consumables suppliers, logistics service providers, and contract manufacturers; develop risk mitigation strategies (dual-sourcing, safety stock optimization) to ensure supply continuity.
 Identify any performance deficiencies and problems or opportunities for improvement in these areas of responsibility and take initiative to solve the problems and realize the opportunities.
 Identify specific cost reduction opportunities and take action to achieve cost reductions, or improve cost effectiveness, including introducing alternative sources where appropriate.
 Work effectively in co-operation with the Production Manager to develop and maintain efficient planning and operations in production, warehousing and materials handling.
 Drive for continuous inventory improvement and implement best practice models to ensure targets are achieved.
 Champion sustainability and ESG initiatives within the supply chain, supporting environmental practices such as packaging reduction.
 Drive digital transformation of materials management processes through automation, data analytics, and system integration to improve forecast accuracy and decision-making speed.
 Qualifications/Requirements: 
 Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Engineering, Business Administration, or related field; master’s degree or APICS/SCMP certification preferred.
 5+ years’ material management experience in a manufacturing setting.
 Strong logistics, supply chain, and material management skills; exposure to JIT, Kanban, MRP, and Lean manufacturing.
 Contract manufacturing / outsourced (EMS/CM) forecasting and supply management experience.
 Hands-on technical depth: SAP, Excel, VBA, Power Query, Smartsheet. Able to build, maintain, document, and troubleshoot tools and processes.
 Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams and setting/meeting aggressive targets.
 Self-motivated, high-energy, results-oriented; forward-thinking and proactive.
 Flexible and adaptable: Open to change and modification of tasks.
 Operational finance knowledge.
 Proven ability to drive change in a matrix environment.
 Ability to successfully motivate and maintain employee involvement while driving change.
 Desired Characteristics: 
 Ability to translate complex supply chain data into clear executive-level presentations and stakeholder communications.
 Experience navigating supplier negotiations in volatile commodity markets or constrained supply environments.
 Strong root-cause analysis skills applied to supply disruptions, quality escapes, and delivery failures.
 Track record of leading cross-functional supply chain improvement projects (e.g., ERP migrations, warehouse redesigns, supplier consolidation).
 Familiarity with demand sensing, predictive analytics, or AI-driven planning tools.
 Knowledge of sustainability frameworks and experience integrating ESG criteria into supplier selection.

1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

As a Staff Security Engineer on Security Incident Response, you'll serve as a senior technical leader and builder for the team, helping shape both how we respond to incidents today and how our response capabilities evolve over time.This role is about advancing what the team is capable of, not just responding when something breaks. You'll design and build the AI-assisted systems that extend the team's reach, lead the response to the most complex incidents, and own programs that make the organization more prepared over time, from tabletop exercises and gamedays to the continued advancement of threat hunting and insider risk capabilities.

You bring engineering depth, sound incident judgment, and the ability to plan, and deliver complex work against a longer-term maturity roadmap not just execute against a queue.

This is a senior individual contributor role with organization-wide impact on how 1Password investigates, contains, and learns from security incidents.

This role reports to the Manager, Security Incident Response.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

What we're looking for:

 - Significant experience leading complex, high-severity security incidents across multiple environments, including serving as an incident commander or equivalent technical lead.

 - Experience designing and building AI-assisted or agentic automation for security operations (triage, investigation, containment), with sound judgment about where automation should and shouldn't hold decision authority.

 - Strong software engineering skills, and experience building production tooling, automation, or systems rather than only operating existing security platforms.

 - Experience owning a security program or capability roadmap end to end, including planning, sequencing, and delivering multi-quarter work.

 - Strong understanding of cloud-native, SaaS, and identity-driven attack techniques and response approaches.

 - Experience designing and running tabletop exercises, gamedays, or comparable readiness programs and translating findings into improvements..

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to represent technical tradeoffs to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

 - Experience mentoring engineers or otherwise raising the technical and investigative capabilities of a team.

How you'll work:

 - You look for opportunities to build systems that scale the team's capabilities rather than relying on repeated manual effort, and you're interested in thoughtfully applying AI and automation where they can improve security outcomes.

 - An experienced incident commander who brings structure to complex incidents, makes sound decisions with incomplete information, and helps teams move forward during high-pressure situations.

 - You're comfortable taking ownership of a capability from strategy through execution, including defining priorities, sequencing work, navigating dependencies, and delivering against a longer-term roadmap.

 - You can operate as a technical partner to leaders and cross-functional teams, independently representing technical priorities, risks, and tradeoffs.

 - You value continuous improvement and contribute to an environment where teams can examine incidents, decisions, and failures openly and turn what they learn into stronger systems and practices.

What you can expect:

 - Serve as incident manager and technical escalation point for complex, high-severity events, bringing structure, sound judgement, and clear decision-making under pressure.

 - Design and build AI-assisted and automated systems that improve how quickly and consistently the team can triage, investigate, and contain incidents.

 - Establish appropriate safety controls, approval gates, auditability, and rollback mechanisms for automated and AI-assisted actions, ensuring high-impact decisions remain appropriately human-controlled.

 - Own the team's readiness programs, including tabletop exercises and incident gamedays, from scenario design and execution through debriefing and translating finishes into concrete (or measurable) improvements

 - Advance the team’s threat hunting and insider risk capabilities by identifying opportunities, defining priorities, and delivering roadmap work that improves investigative depth and coverage

 - Plan, sequence, and deliver multi-quarter initiatives that mature the team's capabilities, bringing project management discipline to work that doesn't fit neatly into a sprint.

 - Mentor and provide technical leadership to other engineers, strengthening engineering rigor and investigative judgement across the team.

 - Partner with Security Operations, Product Security, and Engineering teams to close gaps surfaced through investigations, hunting, and simulations.

 - Foster psychological safety and blameless learning across incident retrospectives, gamedays, and tabletop debriefs.

 - Extend strong incident response practices beyond the immediate team by building reusable systems, tooling, and operating patterns that strengthen response capabilities across areas such as PSIRT, Privacy, and Engineering.

 Expérience dans le développement de logiciels pour des systèmes embarqués, des appareils en périphérie (edge), des appliances ou d’autres environnements présentant des contraintes similaires

Chez nous, le jeu est une affaire sérieuse. Nous sommes à la recherche d’aventurières et d’aventuriers curieux, prêts à trouver leur groupe, animés par l’imagination et la détermination de concevoir ce qui n’a encore jamais été conçu. Chez Hasbro et Wizards of the Coast, vous collaborerez avec des équipes passionnées afin de réinventer nos marques emblématiques et de créer des expériences qui suscitent la joie, le sentiment d’appartenance et l’esprit de communauté grâce à la magie du jeu. C’est votre occasion de contribuer à façonner un jeu légendaire qui dure toute une vie.
 Aperçu du poste
 Joignez-vous à Hasbro à titre de spécialiste des systèmes dans le cadre d’un remplacement de congé de maternité (12 mois) et devenez un maillon essentiel de notre équipe novatrice à Longueuil (Québec), au Canada. Cette occasion exceptionnelle vous permettra de participer au développement, à l’amélioration, à la mise à l’essai et à la maintenance des environnements système qui soutiennent notre développement créatif et de produits.  Lieu et modalités de travail
 Ce poste est basé à notre bureau de Montréal (Québec), au Canada, et suit un horaire hybride conçu pour favoriser la collaboration en personne. Les membres du personnel doivent travailler sur place les mardis, mercredis et jeudis, et ont la flexibilité de travailler à distance ou sur place les lundis et vendredis.
 Vos responsabilités
 Développer, améliorer et mettre à l’essai des flux de travail automatisés soutenant le développement de produits ainsi que de ressources numériques et imprimées.
 Soutenir les tests d’acceptation par les utilisateurs (UAT) des flux de travail nouveaux ou mis à jour en corrigeant les erreurs et en mettant en œuvre les demandes de modification des testeuses et testeurs.
 Proposer et élaborer des solutions, au moyen de tableaux de bord de données, afin d’aider les utilisatrices et utilisateurs quotidiens des systèmes à gérer leur charge de travail et à mesurer leur rendement.
 Créer des requêtes de recherche pour extraire des données des systèmes afin d’alimenter les rapports élaborés ou utilisés par les utilisatrices et utilisateurs quotidiens ainsi que par les analystes de données.

 Repérer de nouvelles fonctionnalités des systèmes qui permettraient d’accroître l’efficacité des utilisatrices et utilisateurs quotidiens, puis les communiquer aux gestionnaires de processus et aux spécialistes du contenu numérique.

 Excellentes habiletés analytiques et capacité à résoudre des problèmes.
 Capacité à comprendre des processus complexes et à les transformer en flux de travail automatisés.
 Sens de l’organisation et grand souci du détail.
 Capacité à établir l’ordre de priorité de tâches concurrentes et à respecter les échéances.
 Autonomie, motivation personnelle et esprit novateur.
 Bonnes habiletés en communication et en relations interpersonnelles.
 Un baccalauréat en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe, ou une expérience équivalente.

About Behavox 
 About the Role 
 The Senior FP&A Analyst owns Behavox's core financial model — its architecture, the accounting beneath it, and the forecasts and analysis the company plans and decides by. The role exists to change decisions, not report them: it turns the numbers into the choices leadership actually faces. It reads and integrates budgets into the model, but does not run the budgeting cycle.
 The same analyst builds the valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma models behind every acquisition — evaluating targets, running diligence, and folding closed deals into a single consolidated view. This work is periodic and must be carried alone when it arrives; the steady state is the operating model and SaaS forecasting.
 This is a high-autonomy role that works without a detailed brief and sets the modeling standard others build on. It is accountable for the accuracy and integrity of the numbers, and for turning them into recommendations sharp enough to act on — the downside case included, not just the point estimate — for senior leadership, the board, and investors. It pressure-tests the assumptions behind every result, works fluently with modern tooling and AI, and compounds that edge by learning relentlessly. Its influence comes from the rigor and reach of the analysis, not from authority: it owns the model and the truth it tells, not the decisions made from it.
 What You'll Bring 
 Financial Model & Accounting Foundations — Understands the architecture of integrated three-statement and operating models and the accounting that underpins them, including SaaS revenue recognition and cost treatment. Understands how the company's budgets are built and how to integrate them accurately into the core financial model.
 Forecasting & SaaS Unit Economics — Understands bottom-up short-term forecasting, driver-based long-term modeling, and the SaaS metrics that reveal business performance. Connects movements in those metrics to their underlying drivers and the operating levers that can change them.
 Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration — Understands acquisition valuation, purchase accounting, combined-entity projections, and consolidation mechanics sufficiently to evaluate targets and integrate completed acquisitions into the financial model.
 Business & Commercial Acumen — Understands in depth how the business and its functions generate revenue and incur costs, including the underlying revenue drivers, cost structure, and operating levers. Applies this knowledge to identify inconsistencies and challenge financial results and assumptions.
 Financial Systems & AI Tooling — Understands Google Sheets, Excel, AI, and automation capabilities sufficiently to determine how they should be applied to financial modeling and analysis. Distinguishes where automation can improve speed and control from where financial judgment and manual validation must remain.
 What You'll Do 
 Financial Model Ownership — Builds and maintains the core three-statement and operating model using robust architecture, accounting logic, scenario and sensitivity layers, and integrated budgets, owning the accuracy of every output and the integrity of every assumption to provide reliable forecasts and analysis for company planning and decision-making.
 Acquisition Modeling & Integration — Builds valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma combined-entity models by independently evaluating targets, supporting due diligence, and consolidating closed deals to provide a complete financial view of acquisition implications and the combined business.
 Business-Review Reporting — Drives the financial substance of monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews with the broader FP&A team by translating model outputs and performance drivers into a clear narrative that enables senior management, the board, and investors to understand results and their implications.
 Metrics Analysis & Business Partnering — Diagnoses financial and SaaS metric movements by identifying operating drivers, pressure-testing assumptions, and modeling relevant levers and downside cases to give decision-makers evidence-based recommendations they can act on.
 AI-Enabled Productivity — Applies AI and spreadsheet automation to recurring financial workflows by automating appropriate work and strengthening data validation while retaining judgment over what remains manual to reduce cycle time without compromising financial integrity.
 What We Offer 
 A highly attractive benefits package, including competitive cash compensation, and an equity award aligned with long-term value creation.
 Modern, comfortable offices in Toronto and Montreal. This is a hybrid role (3 days in office).

During the process we will begin by exploring the core factors regarding salary and location along with core experience and skills and values alignment. We will then deep dive explore the critical technical competencies we have identified for the role, and then we will deep dive in behavioral competencies.

 Job Description 
 The Director, Issuing Solutions Sales & Business Development, Canada will be responsible for accelerating the growth of Visa's Value-Added Services business across the Canadian market. 
 This is a client-facing commercial role combining sales, business development, market development and consultative solution selling. The Director will identify new opportunities, build qualified pipeline, develop senior client relationships, shape solutions and actively advance opportunities through the sales cycle to deliver commercial outcomes. 
 The successful candidate will operate at the intersection of client strategy, technology and sales execution. They will engage Canadian issuers to understand strategic priorities and business challenges, identify whitespace, lead client discovery, develop compelling business cases and solution strategies, and bring together the appropriate Visa capabilities to address client needs. 
 Working closely with Visa's Account Executives, Specialist Sellers, Product, Visa Consulting & Analytics (VCA), Solutions Engineering and other cross-functional partners, this individual will help clients navigate opportunities across Visa's evolving portfolio while maintaining clear accountability for pipeline creation, sales execution and revenue growth. 
 The role requires a hands-on commercial leader who is equally comfortable creating an opportunity, shaping the solution and selling the value proposition. 
 Essential Functions 
 Sales & Commercial Execution 
 Develop, own and advance a pipeline of Issuing Solutions opportunities across Canada, with accountability for revenue growth and commercial outcomes. 
 Lead client engagements throughout the sales cycle, including prospecting, discovery, opportunity qualification, solution positioning, business-case development, commercial discussions and close. 
 Build and maintain senior-level relationships across existing and prospective Canadian issuer clients. 
 Proactively uncover new client needs and translate those needs into actionable sales opportunities. 
 Develop compelling value propositions and commercial narratives that connect Visa capabilities to measurable client business outcomes. 
 Partner closely with Visa Account Executives and Specialist Sellers to establish account strategies, coordinate client engagement and progress opportunities. 
 Maintain strong sales discipline around pipeline management, forecasting, opportunity progression, risks and next steps. 
 Client Discovery & Solution Development 
 Lead structured client discovery to understand strategic priorities, operational challenges, technology environments and modernization needs. 
 Translate client challenges into integrated solution strategies across Visa's broader portfolio rather than approaching clients solely through individual products. 
 Develop client-specific business cases that clearly articulate strategic value, expected outcomes and commercial rationale. 
 Provide consultative and technical sales leadership throughout complex opportunities, engaging product and technical specialists when deeper solution expertise is required. 
 Help bridge client strategy, business requirements, Visa capabilities and technical feasibility to accelerate opportunities through the decision-making process. 
 Navigate complex client environments involving multiple decision-makers and business and technology stakeholders. 
 Canada Market Development & Go-to-Market 
 Identify whitespace across Visa's Canadian issuer relationships and translate that whitespace into targeted commercial opportunities. 
 Develop account-level and market-level go-to-market strategies reflecting the unique structure and dynamics of the Canadian payments ecosystem. 
 Create qualified opportunities across Pismo, Verifi, VCA, fraud and risk, digital enablement, network solutions, post-purchase experiences and other relevant Visa capabilities. 
 Develop executive relationships that position Visa as a strategic business and technology partner. 
 Identify emerging client needs and market trends and translate those insights into actionable sales strategies. 
 Bring Canadian market and client insights back into Visa to help inform commercialization strategies, product priorities and future go-to-market approaches. 
 Work across Visa's broader organization to create coordinated client strategies and bring the appropriate resources and expertise to priority opportunities.  
 Leadership Profile 
 The ideal candidate will combine the commercial drive of a seller, the structured thinking of a consultant and the solution orientation of a sales engineer. 
 This individual should be comfortable walking into an issuer with an open-ended business challenge, leading discovery, identifying where Visa has a credible right to play, developing the business case, mobilizing product and technical expertise, advancing commercial discussions and ultimately helping close the business.

 Building and converting a healthy pipeline of Canadian Issuing Solutions opportunities. 
 Generating new sales and contributing directly to Canada revenue objectives. 
 Identifying previously untapped whitespace within Visa's issuer relationships. 
 Converting discovery and strategic client conversations into qualified commercial opportunities. 
 Developing strong executive relationships across priority Canadian financial institutions. 
 Building compelling business cases and solution strategies for larger, complex or multi-solution opportunities. 
 Accelerating commercial opportunities across Pismo, Verifi, VCA and Visa's broader Value-Added Services portfolio. 
 Strengthening coordination across Account Executives, Specialist Sales, Product, VCA and technical teams. 
 Establishing a scalable foundation for continued growth of Visa's Issuing Solutions business in Canada. 
 Qualifications 
 Basic Qualifications 
 Significant experience in sales, business development, market development, management consulting, solution engineering, financial services, payments, fintech or enterprise technology. 
 Demonstrated experience developing and advancing complex B2B sales opportunities. 
 Proven ability to establish and maintain relationships with senior client executives and key decision-makers. 
 Strong commercial orientation with experience identifying potential opportunities, developing value propositions and progressing opportunities through a structured sales process. 
 Experience leading client discovery and translating complex business challenges into actionable solutions and business cases. 
 Ability to understand technically complex products and effectively connect technology capabilities to business outcomes.

 Demonstrated ability to operate successfully in a highly matrixed organization and influence across teams without direct authority. 
 Preferred Qualifications

 Experience working directly with financial institutions, issuers, payment processors, fintechs or technology platforms.

 Experience selling or developing opportunities involving payments technology, issuer processing, digital payments, fraud and risk, consulting or other enterprise technology solutions.

À propos d'Elia
elia est une plateforme SaaS B2B de gestion de l'espace de travail qui aide les entreprises à
réinventer leur environnement de travail : réservation de bureaux et de salles, gestion des
visiteurs, capteurs IoT et occupation, gestion d'actifs, affichage numérique, casiers
intelligents, et plus encore. Nos clients incluent de grandes organisations à travers le Canada,
les États-Unis et quelques autres pays.
 
Nous concevons nous-mêmes une bonne partie du matériel qui alimente la plateforme :
capteurs d'occupation, casiers intelligents et autres équipements connectés. Nous sommes
une équipe technique, en pleine croissance, où chaque personne a un impact direct sur le
produit et où l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de construire.
 
Le rôle
Nous cherchons un·e ingénieur·e électronique pour concevoir et faire évoluer les produits
matériels d'elia, de la feuille blanche jusqu'à la production. Vous travaillerez dans l'équipe
hardware pour apporter des idées jusqu'à des produits fiables, assurés chez nos clients.
 
On cherche quelqu'un qui aime avoir les mains dans le design de circuit électronique autant
que de participer aux décisions techniques sur la conception de produit, quelqu'un qui pose
les bonnes questions, qui n'a pas peur de challenger nos choix techniques (ni de se faire
challenger), et qui veut continuellement apprendre et s'améliorer.
 
Responsabilités
Concevoir les circuits électroniques de nos produits : schématiques et layout de PCB.
Sélectionnez les composants en tenant compte de la performance, du coût, de la
disponibilité et du cycle de vie.
Prototypeur, assembleur, testeur et déboguer les cartes, puis documenter les résultats.
Faire les choix techniques d'architecture matérielle (alimentation, communication sans fil,
capteurs, microcontrôleurs, etc.).
Participer activement aux décisions techniques sur le produit, en collaboration avec les
membres multidisciplinaires de l'équipe hardware.
Travailler avec les fabricants et assembleurs (DFM, DFT) pour amener les produits en
production
Contribuer à la conception sécuritaire de nos équipements connectés.
Proposer des améliorations continue à nos processus de conception, de test et de
validation
 
Profil recherché
BAC en génie électrique ou génie électronique
Minimum 3 ans d'expérience en conception électronique
Expérience concrète en schématique et layout de PCB
Expérience en test et débogage de cartes : oscilloscope, analyseur logique, multimètre,
alimentation de laboratoire
Bonnes connaissances des microcontrôleurs (ESP32, nRF ou équivalent) et des interfaces
courantes (I2C, SPI, UART, USB)
Connaissance de la conception d'alimentations et de circuits basse consommation
Expérience avec les communications sans fil (BLE, Wi-Fi ou autre), un atout
Capacité à écrire du firmware de base pour tester et valider les circuits conçus, un atout
Curiosité technique, toujours vouloir en apprendre plus, à s'améliorer
Capacité à synthétiser de l'information complexe et à la vulgariser
 
À l'aise avec l'IA
Chez Elia, l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de travailler. On ne cherche pas à vous
convaincre que l'IA accélère le travail. En partie du principe que vous le savez déjà. Ce qu'on
recherche :
Vous utilisez déjà Claude (ou un outil équivalent) au quotidien, pour la recherche de
composants, la lecture de fiches techniques, l'analyse de résultats de tests ou pour repenser
votre façon de travailler;
Vous êtes capable de nous montrer une façon différente de faire les choses, pas
seulement de suivre le mouvement;
 
Ce que nous offrons
Chez elia, tu auras l'opportunité de :
Travailler dans une équipe dynamique en pleine croissance;
Vivre l'expérience « start-up » et voir tes conceptions installées chez de grands clients;
Profiter d'un horaire flexible;
Ayez un accès gratuit au Tonic Gym ou 100$ pour faire du sport;
Participant à nos fameux G-PHEST;
Avoir accès à des assurances collectives;

 Minimum de 5 ans d’expérience en installation mécanique de lignes d’arbres, turbines ou générateurs
 Excellentes compétences informatiques et bonne maîtrise de MS Office

OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring Float's first Staff Security Engineer, to own the technical direction of our security platform: application, infrastructure and identity security. Our security team is small and builds more than it buys. We write our own detections, run our own agent platform, and fix things at the root. Float's engineers build quickly and we don't run big security gates, so your job is to make the secure path the easy one. You'll take a complex area of security, own it from end to end, and design the fixes alongside engineering, then drive them through to adoption across product teams. You'll look ahead too, setting up the foundations for new products, and for how we run AI tools safely, well before teams start building. You'll work as a peer to our staff and principal engineers, and explain big architectural changes and the risk behind them in a way that moves everyone toward the outcome.

WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Own the technical strategy for security platform work: set standards, write down decisions, and explain risk to leadership in business terms.

 - Own a major area of security end to end, from the risks and the plan through to shipped improvements.

 - Build security primitives into our core backend (Python and Django), such as default-closed authorization and tenancy scoping, then lead adoption across every product team.

 - Shape our customer identity platform: passwords, passkeys, SSO/SAML and machine-to-machine authentication.

 - Threat model and review the architecture and code of new products and large changes, and help redesign things so they are better, not only point out what's wrong.

 - Secure how we use AI: our internal agent platform, MCP gateways, and the data that flows through them.

 - Look ahead and put security foundations in place about six months before teams start building in a new area.

 - Lead multi-quarter efforts across several engineers as the security voice in the room, with minimal drag on engineering delivery, and mentor engineers on and off the security team.

 - Present significant architectural and engineering changes, with the risks, to engineers and leaders so they understand and act.

 - Harden our CI/CD and software supply chain, and turn controls into code (infrastructure as code, policy as code) instead of manual work.

 - Help secure the platform as we move to Kubernetes: workload isolation, network policy, IAM and secrets.

 - Build in-house tools and capabilities where it makes more sense than buying them as Float grows.

 - Give timely, practical advice early in the process so teams spend less time waiting on security.

 - Identify blind spots across the company and help set priorities for where security should invest.

 - Use AI tools to move faster on threat modelling, reviews, investigation and building.

ABOUT YOU

Here's what sets you up for success at Float:

 - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.

 - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.

 - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.

 - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.

 - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work.

 - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.

elia est la plateforme tout-en-un d'opérations des espaces de travail des grandes organisations. Réservation de bureaux et de salles, gestion des visiteurs, capteurs d'occupation, casiers intelligents, affichage numérique, gestion d'actifs : on réunit tout dans une seule plateforme. Chaque personne a un impact direct sur le produit et sur la façon dont on bâtit l'entreprise, et l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de travailler.
Le rôle
Demandez à n'importe qui qui gère les bureaux d'une grande organisation à quoi ressemble sa semaine : salles de réunion réservées en double, bureaux vides le vendredi et pris d'assaut le mercredi, visiteurs qui attendent à l'accueil parce que personne ne les attendait, cinq outils différents qui ne se parlent pas.
elia règle ça avec une seule plateforme pour les équipes qui gèrent le milieu de travail : gestion des installations, TI et RH. Certaines des plus grandes organisations privées et publiques du Québec roulent déjà leur milieu de travail sur elia, et nous voulons rejoindre les prochaines.
Comme SDR, vous ouvrez la porte. Vous appelez des gens dans de grandes organisations du Québec, vous amorcez de vraies conversations sur la façon dont leur milieu de travail fonctionne, et vous obtenez les appels découverte que nos Account Executives transforment en contrats. C'est un poste d'appels à froid en grand volume, principalement en français.
Responsabilités
Faire un grand volume d'appels à froid chaque jour auprès d'une liste définie de grandes organisations du Québec (500 employés et plus), principalement en français.
Utiliser le téléphone comme canal principal, appuyé par le courriel et LinkedIn.
Faire de la recherche sur chaque compte avant de le contacter, pour que chaque appel ait une vraie raison d'être.
Obtenir des appels découverte avec les bonnes personnes en gestion des installations, milieu de travail, immobilier, TI et RH.
Rédiger une note de transfert claire pour chaque appel : qui y participe, quel problème la personne a probablement, et pourquoi maintenant.
S'assurer que les prospects se présentent, et programmer l'appel au besoin.
Travailler de près avec nos Account Executives du Québec pour choisir les comptes à cibler chaque mois.
Garder HubSpot à jour (« Si ce n'est pas dans le CRM, ça n'est pas arrivé »).

Excellent français, parlé et écrit, naturel au téléphone. Vous passerez vos journées en appels avec des décideurs québécois, et l'aisance en français fait une différence visible dans les résultats.

Idéalement, de l'expérience en appels à froid ou en prospection : rôle de SDR, télémarketing, recrutement, ventes internes (peu importe l'industrie, vous n'avez pas besoin de connaître la nôtre).

À l'aise au téléphone toute la journée : vous appelez les gens, vous ne vous cachez pas derrière le courriel.

Curiosité pour le fonctionnement des entreprises, et discipline de faire vos recherches d'abord.

C'est la première marche d'une échelle de carrière en vente qui est publiée, pas un cul-de-sac. Le parcours est défini par une formule, pas par une opinion : les SDR progressent à travers cinq niveaux avec des cibles claires, puis passent à Sales Associate, où vous êtes responsable de vos propres ventes et les concluez, et ensuite à Account Executive. Un horaire flexible.
Un accès gratuit au Tonic Gym ou 100 $ pour faire du sport.
Participer à nos fameux G-PHEST.
Un accès à des assurances collectives.

 Le directeur ou la directrice, Stratégie des appels d’offres et tarification, dirige la façon dont Lyft Urban Solutions repère, élabore et remporte de nouvelles affaires. Ce poste réunit au sein d’une même fonction la stratégie commerciale, l’intelligence d’affaires, la planification de la demande et la gestion des appels d’offres. À titre de partenaire stratégique et de bras droit du chef de la stratégie commerciale et de la livraison, la personne titulaire pilote l'entièreté du cycle de poursuite des occasions d’affaires soit de la stratégie de marché et du positionnement avant les appels d’offres jusqu’au dépôt des soumissions et au transfert aux équipes de réalisation. Nous recherchons un ou une stratège aussi solide sur les plans commercial, technique et financier, qui dirige avec assurance ses équipes et des équipes multifonctionnelles.
 Lyft Solutions Urbaines (souvent appelé LUS) crée des programmes de vélos et de trottinettes en libre-service que les usagers adorent, dont les villes ont besoin et que les exploitants apprécient. Nous concevons, fabriquons et soutenons les vélos et la technologie des stations qui font fonctionner des programmes de vélopartage dans des villes du monde entier, dont BIXI. Notre équipe de Montréal est au cœur de ce travail : elle réunit sous un même toit les équipes d'ingénierie, de fabrication, de chaîne d'approvisionnement, d'opérations, de marketing et commerciales.
 Responsabilités: 
 Stratégie commerciale, intelligence d’affaires et planification de la demande 
 Définir la stratégie commerciale avec le chef de la stratégie commerciale et de la livraison, notamment les marchés cibles, les régions prioritaires et les priorités de croissance.
 Diriger le ou la gestionnaire, Stratégie commerciale et planification de la demande, en matière de planification, de politique de tarification, d’intelligence d’affaires et de planification de la demande.
 Développer une intelligence d’affaires et une veille sur les appels d’offres (marchés, clients, concurrents et approvisionnement) qui orientent la stratégie, le carnet d’occasions et les décisions de poursuite.
 Assumer la planification de la demande et les prévisions du carnet d’occasions, en arrimant la capacité et les ressources de l’équipe des appels d’offres aux occasions anticipées et aux cibles de revenus.
 Avant l’appel d’offres, capture et décision de soumissionner 
 Responsable du processus à jalons décisionnels que suivent toutes les occasions en avant des appels d’offres, en cohérence avec la stratégie commerciale et les régions cibles.
 Réaliser des plans de capture pour les occasions stratégiques et ciblées, afin de façonner les occasions bien avant la publication des appels d’offres.
 Formuler les recommandations de soumissionner ou non, en présentant à la haute direction une vision claire de l’adéquation stratégique, du chemin vers le succès, des risques et du rendement financier.
 Stratégie et exécution des soumissions 
 Positionner chaque soumission pour gagner : définir dès le lancement les thèmes gagnants, la proposition de valeur, les éléments de différenciation concurrentielle et le positionnement tarifaire.
 Façonner les solutions et les offres commerciales avec les équipes d’exploitation, techniques, des finances et des affaires juridiques, afin qu’elles soient concurrentielles, réalisables et rentables.
 Élaborer et remettre en question les modèles financiers, la tarification et les analyses de rentabilisation des soumissions, en veillant à ce que chaque soumission respecte les seuils de marge convenus.
 Instaurer une planification rigoureuse des soumissions, avec des jalons, des étapes de revue, des responsables et des échéances claires.
 Leadership et partenariats 
 Diriger et faire grandir une équipe composée de gestionnaires d’appels d’offres, de spécialistes, de coordonnateurs et coordonnatrices ainsi que du ou de la gestionnaire, Stratégie commerciale et planification de la demande, comme une seule fonction très performante.
 Diriger avec autorité les équipes multifonctionnelles de soumission et tenir les contributeurs responsables du respect des échéances.
 Prendre des décisions opportunes et assurées en contexte d’ambiguïté, en équilibrant les risques et le potentiel de gain.
 Faire le lien entre les ventes, les appels d’offres, les contrats et la réalisation, afin que ce que nous vendons puisse être livré de façon rentable.
 Expérience: 
 Plus de 12 ans d’expérience dans des rôles liés aux appels d’offres, à la capture d’affaires, au développement commercial ou au développement des affaires, dont plus de 5 ans à diriger des équipes à titre de gestionnaire principal, de directeur ou l’équivalent.
 Sens commercial et des ventes : un historique de succès dans des appels d’offres d’envergure et complexes, et une solide compréhension des cycles de vente, des relations clients et du positionnement de marché.
 Esprit stratégique : capacité à saisir les occasions, à définir la stratégie de soumission et à formuler des recommandations claires à la haute direction.
 Compétences techniques : capacité à comprendre et à façonner des solutions techniques et opérationnelles, à échanger de façon crédible avec les experts et à transformer les exigences en offres convaincantes et réalisables. À l’aise avec les données, l’intelligence d’affaires et les outils de planification.
 Solides compétences financières : maîtrise de la modélisation financière, de la tarification, des états des résultats, des flux de trésorerie et de la gestion des marges, et capacité à défendre les données financières des soumissions auprès des finances et de la haute direction.
 Leadership assuré : capacité à bâtir des équipes très performantes et à influencer les parties prenantes de haut niveau de différentes fonctions.
 Maîtrise professionnelle du français et de l’anglais, à l’oral et à l’écrit (la connaissance d’une troisième langue est un atout). La maîtrise de l’anglais est requise pour collaborer avec les équipes de Lyft, ainsi qu’avec des clients et des partenaires en Amérique du Nord et à l’international.
 Atouts : expérience avec les méthodologies APMP ou Shipley, expérience des appels d’offres dans plusieurs régions et parcours combinant appels d’offres et réalisation.
 À quoi ressemble la réussite (12 premiers mois) 
 Un processus à jalons décisionnels en amont des appels d’offres et des plans de capture en place pour toutes les occasions stratégiques et ciblées.
 Une capacité fonctionnelle d’intelligence d’affaires et de planification de la demande qui oriente les décisions liées au carnet d’occasions et aux ressources.
 Un taux de succès amélioré, chaque soumission reposant sur une stratégie claire et un modèle financier ambitieux mais crédible.
 Une équipe solide et unie, reconnue comme un partenaire de confiance dans l’ensemble de l’organisation.

 DESCRIPTION DU POSTE: 
 Le ou la gestionnaire, Paie internationale, est responsable de la paie de Valsoft à l’extérieur de l’Amérique du Nord : intégrer les entreprises nouvellement acquises à une paie contrôlée et conforme, stabiliser les paies à risque et bâtir un modèle d’équipe et de fournisseurs évolutif à mesure que le portefeuille grandit. Chaque acquisition arrive avec son propre fournisseur de paie, ses propres processus et son propre niveau de contrôle; ce rôle consiste à transformer cette diversité en une opération de paie internationale uniforme et vérifiable, au service de tous les groupes opérationnels de Valsoft. Relevant de la direction, Paie et avantages sociaux, et à la tête d’une équipe de spécialistes de la paie internationale, vous serez responsable de toutes les paies à l’extérieur du Canada et des États-Unis. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec le ou la gestionnaire, Paie et avantages sociaux, responsable de l’Amérique du Nord, afin d’assurer l’uniformité des processus, des contrôles et des rapports à l’échelle mondiale. Ce poste est en présentiel à notre siège social de Montréal. La personne idéale allie pensée stratégique et exécution concrète, a un intérêt marqué pour la conception de processus et l’amélioration continue, et fait preuve d’une grande rigueur en matière de contrôle et de conformité. Vous êtes un(e) leader qui développe son équipe, gère les parties prenantes et les fournisseurs à travers différentes cultures et fuseaux horaires, et traite les données confidentielles avec discrétion.
 RESPONSABILITÉS PRINCIPALES: 
 ·       Définir la stratégie et la feuille de route de la paie internationale, en cohérence avec la croissance par acquisitions de Valsoft.
 ·       Bâtir, diriger et développer l’équipe de paie internationale, en l’élargissant au besoin pour assurer une couverture adéquate dans tous les pays, et établir des objectifs et des indicateurs de performance clairs.
 ·       Diriger l’évaluation et l’intégration de la paie des entreprises internationales acquises, de la vérification diligente jusqu’au régime de croisière.
 ·       Offrir une expertise et des conseils en matière de paie à la haute direction et aux groupes opérationnels.
 ·       Collaborer avec le ou la gestionnaire, Paie et avantages sociaux, afin d’harmoniser les processus, les contrôles et les rapports à l’échelle mondiale.
 ·       Superviser la paie dans tous les pays et veiller à ce qu’elle soit exacte, versée à temps et conforme.
 ·       Assurer la conformité aux lois locales en matière de paie, de fiscalité, de sécurité sociale et d’emploi, et effectuer une veille des changements réglementaires.
 ·       Être responsable de l’exactitude, du respect des échéances et de la révision des rapports de paie, des déclarations réglementaires et des processus de fin d’année dans chaque pays.
 ·       Diriger la prise en charge et la stabilisation des paies internationales à risque.
 ·       Mettre en place une supervision des paies gérées à l’extérieur de l’équipe par des entités locales ou des fournisseurs tiers, au moyen d’un inventaire centralisé, de rapports réguliers, de revues périodiques et d’un processus d’escalade clair, afin que toutes les paies respectent les normes de Valsoft.
 ·       Diriger les audits internes et externes.
 ·       Veiller à ce que les rapprochements de paie et les écritures de journal soient effectués et révisés avec l’équipe des Finances.
 ·       Regrouper les fournisseurs de paie internationaux et gérer leur performance, leurs niveaux de service et leurs coûts.
 ·       Assurer l’intégrité, la sécurité et la confidentialité des données (p. ex. RGPD) dans l’ensemble des systèmes de paie et auprès des fournisseurs.
 ·       Élaborer et tenir à jour les procédures normalisées, les guides et la documentation pour la paie internationale et les intégrations.
 ·       Normaliser et améliorer continuellement les processus et la technologie, en identifiant des économies de coûts et des gains d’efficacité.
 ·       Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les RH, les Finances, le service juridique, les groupes opérationnels et les partenaires externes, notamment sur les politiques internationales ayant une incidence sur la rémunération.
 ·       Résoudre les problèmes de paie complexes et les escalades.
 QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES / MINIMALES: 
 ·       Plus de 7 ans d’expérience en paie, incluant la gestion d’équipe.
 ·       Expérience à la tête de projets d’intégration ou de migration de paie, ou de regroupement de fournisseurs, idéalement dans un environnement d’acquisitions.
 ·       Solide connaissance de la conformité en matière de paie, des contrôles internes et des audits.
 ·       Capacité démontrée à améliorer et à normaliser les processus de paie, en élaborant des procédures et une documentation évolutives.
 ·       Diplôme en comptabilité, en finance, en administration ou en ressources humaines, ou expérience équivalente.
 ·       Maîtrise de l’anglais (vous travaillerez avec des équipes de paie, des fournisseurs et des parties prenantes dans plusieurs pays).

 DESCRIPTION: 
 Valsoft is looking for a Manager, International Payroll to join our Payroll & Benefits team at our Montreal headquarters.
 ABOUT VALSOFT CORP.: 
 Established in Canada in 2015, Valsoft has grown to a global portfolio of 118+ companies, acquiring and developing vertical market software companies, enabling each business to deliver the best mission-critical solutions for customers in their respective industries. A key tenet of Valsoft’s philosophy is to invest in well-established businesses and foster an entrepreneurial environment that molds companies into leaders in their respective industries. Valsoft looks to buy, hold and create value through long-term partnerships with existing management.  
 INVESTMENT APPROACH: 
 Unlike private equity and venture capital firms, we are Entrepreneurs who Buy , Enhance and Grow Software Businesses. That’s right; we don’t sell businesses. We form a strategic alliance with existing management teams. We recognize the dedication and perseverance required to create a firm and place a premium on customers’ and workers’ well-being over short-term goals.   
 CULTURE: 
 Valsoft is more than just a place to work; we’re a team. We mean it when we say people are our greatest assets, so investing in them is our number one priority. We create an environment where our employees feel first-day-on-the-job excitement, day after day, creating a culture of high performers and collaboration. We celebrate our milestones, and we’re proud of them. We Dream Big, Stay Humble and Stay Hungry.  
 POSITION DESCRIPTION: 
 The Manager, International Payroll owns Valsoft's payroll outside North America: bringing newly acquired businesses onto a controlled, compliant payroll, stabilizing payrolls at risk, and building a scalable vendor and team model as the portfolio grows. Each acquisition arrives with its own payroll provider, processes and level of control; this role turns that variety into a consistent, auditable international payroll operation that supports all of Valsoft's operating groups. Reporting to the Director, Payroll & Benefits, and leading a team of international payroll specialists, you will be responsible for all payrolls outside Canada and the U.S. You will partner closely with the Payroll & Benefits Manager, who leads North America, to keep processes, controls and reporting consistent globally. This is an in-office role at our Montreal headquarters. The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, a passion for process design and continuous improvement, and a strong control and compliance mindset. You are a leader who develops your team, manages stakeholders and vendors across cultures and time zones, and handles confidential data with discretion.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 ·       Set the strategy and roadmap for international payroll, aligned with Valsoft's acquisition growth.
 ·       Build, lead and develop the international payroll team, expanding it where needed to ensure adequate coverage across all countries, and set clear goals and KPIs.
 ·       Lead the payroll assessment and integration of acquired international businesses, from due diligence through to steady state.
 ·       Provide payroll expertise and advice to senior management and the operating groups.
 ·       Partner with the Payroll & Benefits Manager to align processes, controls and reporting globally.
 ·       Oversee payroll across all countries, ensuring accurate, timely and compliant pay.
 ·       Ensure compliance with local payroll, tax, social security and employment legislation, and monitor regulatory changes.
 ·       Own the accuracy, timeliness and review of payroll reporting, statutory filings and year-end processes in each country.
 ·       Lead the takeover and stabilization of international payrolls at risk.
 ·       Establish oversight of payrolls managed outside the team by local entities or third-party vendors, through a central inventory, regular reporting, periodic reviews and clear escalation, so all payrolls meet Valsoft's standards.
 ·       Lead internal and external audits.
 ·       Ensure payroll reconciliations and journal entries are completed and reviewed with Finance.
 ·       Consolidate international payroll vendors and manage their performance, service levels and cost.
 ·       Ensure data integrity, security and privacy compliance (e.g. GDPR) across payroll systems and vendors.
 ·       Build and maintain standard procedures, playbooks and documentation for international payroll and integrations.
 ·       Standardize and continuously improve processes and technology, identifying cost savings and efficiency gains.
 ·       Work closely with HR, Finance, Legal, the operating groups and external partners, including on international policies that affect pay.
 ·       Resolve complex payroll issues and escalations.
 REQUIRED/MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: 
 ·       7+ years of payroll experience, including team leadership.
 ·       Experience leading payroll integrations, migrations or vendor consolidation, ideally in an acquisitive environment.
 ·       Strong knowledge of payroll compliance, internal controls and audits.
 ·       Proven ability to improve and standardize payroll processes, building procedures and documentation that scale.
 ·       Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or HR, or equivalent experience.
 ·       Fluent English (you will work with payroll teams, vendors and stakeholders across multiple countries).

 Do You Turn Great Creative Direction Into Finished, On-Style Product Art? 
 At Hadley Designs, we believe that learning should be enjoyable, engaging, and screen-free. Millions of parents and teachers trust our beautifully designed, developmentally aligned educational tools to help children grow and thrive. As a fast-growing, family-founded brand, we are on a mission to make learning meaningful for families around the world, and we are looking for an early-career illustrator who wants to spend their days making the art that goes into our products.
 We are seeking a Junior Product Illustrator to work hand-in-hand with our Chief Creative Officer, taking her creative direction and carrying it through to finished, production-ready product art. This is a maker's seat, not a template-and-layout role. If you love to draw, you have a genuine eye for cute, playful, kid-friendly design, and you want to grow your craft inside a brand that ships beautiful products every month, this is a rare opportunity to build your portfolio while doing work that reaches millions of families.
 About Hadley Designs 
 Hadley Designs is redefining early education with creativity and purpose. Every product we create is hand-drawn and teacher-designed, crafted with care to build confidence and connection. Our screen-free tools help families and teachers make learning fun and meaningful, nurturing curiosity and creativity in children. 
 Our Mission: We design screen-free products that parents can trust to help their children learn, grow, and reach their full potential. We create beautifully designed, developmentally sound tools that replace noise and distraction with connection, curiosity, and real learning. 
 Our Vision: We aim to build the most trusted children's brand in the world, present in millions of homes, reshaping how families learn, connect, and grow. Our products will be so widely used and passed down that generations of children will grow up learning from them and choose them again for their own families.
 Role Overview 
 As our Junior Product Illustrator, your one job is to turn the Chief Creative Officer's vision into finished, on-style product art, so Hadley Designs launches new products faster and our creative capacity is multiplied, not capped by a single set of hands. The CCO sets the tone, the style, and the strategy; you carry the hands-on execution, creating new artwork, completing sets in an established style, and building each concept out to production-ready. This is a deliberately early-career seat for someone with real illustration talent who wants to keep growing that craft. You will not be expected to arrive as a seasoned art director. You will be expected to draw well, learn our style quickly, take direction cleanly, and finish the last mile of the creative so the CCO can stay focused on setting direction rather than executing it.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Original Illustration & Artwork 
 Create new artwork and complete sets in Hadley Designs' established style across our product lines.
 Draw and illustrate original elements like characters, motifs, patterns, and scenes that fit our cute, kid-friendly aesthetic.
 Product Design Execution 
 Turn the CCO's concepts and creative direction into finished, production-ready product designs.
 Carry a design from initial handoff through final build-out without kicking work back up the chain.
 Creative Production Support 
 Own the execution offload (variations, building out a design across a full set, and file prep) that frees the CCO's hands.
 Prepare print and production files to spec, and build mockups and product previews for listings.
 Style Consistency 
 Keep every piece on-style and on-brand across the full product set. 
 Maintain the living style-reference so the look stays consistent as the catalog grows.
 As-needed: occasional ad-ops support (A+ content, storefront updates, CMYK ad images) and revisions on existing product lines. This is secondary support, not the core of the role.
 How Success Is Measured 
 First-pass approval rate: the share of deliverables the CCO accepts with no major rework. This is how we measure "on-style" objectively.
 New original art created: the volume of original artwork generated to feed the product pipeline.
 Sets / SKUs completed : finished design sets shipped per month. The speed lever.
 On-time delivery: the share of assigned pieces delivered by the agreed deadline.
 Framework-to-finish independence: the share of projects carried from CCO handoff to production-ready without kicking work back up.
 Who You Are 
 You are an early-career illustrator with genuine drawing talent and a real eye for cute, playful, kid-friendly design. You love to make art and you want to keep doing exactly that. This is the work you want to grow in, not a stepping stone into something else. You take creative direction cleanly, you learn a style fast, and you can carry a piece all the way to finished without needing it handed back to you. You thrive in a remote, fast-moving environment where new products ship every month, and you are excited to build your portfolio inside a brand that reaches millions of families.
 Must-haves 
 A portfolio of original illustration work that shows a cute, playful, kid-friendly or product-design sensibility.
 Working proficiency in Adobe Illustrator for native illustration (not just file handling or layout).
 Ability to match and extend an existing art style, completing a set so new pieces sit naturally alongside the originals.
 Strong ability to take written and verbal creative direction and turn it into finished work.
 Reliability on deadlines while managing several pieces at once.
 Nice-to-haves 
 Experience preparing print / production files to spec.
 Familiarity with the children's, educational, or consumer-product space.
 Comfort with lightweight project tools (Notion, ClickUp) and file organization.
 Note: this is an entry-level maker's role. We are not looking for a senior art director or a veteran illustrator. We are looking for real talent early in its arc, with the interest and hunger to grow.
 Why You'll Love Working Here 
 Impact: Your work will directly impact how families experience learning through the Hadley Designs brand.
 Culture : Join a passionate, mission-driven team that values trust, creativity, and collaboration.
 Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of a remote role with flexible working hours.
 Growth: Learn directly from our Chief Creative Officer and build a portfolio of shipped, real-world product work.
 Remote-first work environment
 Paid time off and holidays
 Access to learning resources and professional development
 Free access to Hadley Designs products
 Regular interaction with leadership, including the CEO and CCO
 Stability from a decade as a family-founded, mission-driven brand
 Apply Today 
 If you're ready to make a meaningful impact in a growing company that's shaping the future of learning, apply now to join the Hadley Designs team as our Junior Product Illustrator. Help us create a lasting impact on families, educators, and children worldwide.

 Responsibilities 
 Month-End Close and Financial Reporting:

 Direct and review the work of our external bookkeeper, ensuring close deadlines and quality standards are met.
 Prepare and reconcile intercompany charges and shared-cost allocations with the counterpart entity, partnering with the other Senior Financial Analyst to keep both sets of books aligned.
 Manage multi-currency accounting, including foreign currency transactions and month-end FX revaluation.
 Prepare monthly management reporting and support budgeting, forecasting, year-end audit, and external tax advisor requests.
 Revenue and Order-to-Cash:

 Ensure revenue is recognized in compliance with ASC 606, including technical analysis of new products and complex enterprise customer contracts.
 Maintain billing system integrity (e.g., Chargebee) and reconcile billing data to the general ledger.

 Execute domestic and international multi-currency payments (ACH, wire, SWIFT, SEPA), including payee banking verification and payment fraud controls.

 Prepare monthly payroll and contractor payments, including Employer of Record (EOR) funding and reconciliation, and maintain contractor documentation (W-9, W-8BEN, 1099).

 Tax and Compliance: 
 Prepare U.S. multi-state sales and use tax filings and maintain tax engine configuration (e.g., Avalara).
 Prepare state registrations, annual reports, franchise tax filings, and other corporate compliance filings for management review.
 Coordinate year-end information returns (1099) and support external advisors with federal and state income tax return preparation.
 Maintain the entity's compliance calendar and ensure all filing deadlines are met.
 Business Partnering:

 Create and update process documentation (SOPs) and training material, and provide training to finance and cross-functional team members.
 Collaborate with the counterpart Senior Financial Analyst to keep processes, policies, and controls consistent across both entities, and provide coverage during absences.

 Process Improvement and Automation:

About us:  
 At Red Rabbit Robotics, our mission is to tackle the global labor shortage and create a future of abundance. We aim to deploy one million humanoid robots in the next 10 years. Our robots are designed to tackle manual labor across manufacturing, warehouse, logistics and more. Our “teleoperation first” strategy immediately delivers value by providing humanoid labor as a service through remote operators, while simultaneously building a powerful data flywheel that fuels the foundation models for robotics and leads to full autonomy for physical world AI.
 Founded just a few months ago, we have already built two generations of humanoid robot prototypes, secured venture backing, and attracted major customers eager to try out our solution. With real time human oversight and a powerful data flywheel, we are building embodied AI systems that can work in the real world in the same way as we do. Check out our prototype demo videos at www.redrabbitrobotics.ai .
 What we believe: 
 We are all about our customers. We talk to real folks in the industry to find out what they actually need, then we build products that solve those problems. Simple as that.
 We are agnostic to different technical approaches. There is no single “silver bullet” for real world robotics. We stay open-minded, keep learning, and try whatever works best.
 We keep it practical. For example, our robots have wheels, not legs (no backflips in the near future). We don’t waste time over-engineering fancy features that don’t make a real difference for our customers’ success.
 The role: 
 We’re looking for a Robotics Engineer to own the design and implementation of our humanoid robot’s control systems. A major responsibility in this role is helping us evaluate and select the right technology stack. You’ll be deeply involved in real-time control loops, sensor fusion, actuator integration, and higher-level motion planning algorithms. This role is in person for our Vancouver, Canada office.

 Design, implement, and optimize real-time control architectures (manipulation, navigation, teleoperation).
 Investigate and compare frameworks and algorithms to guide our core software platform decisions.
 Integrate sensors (LiDAR, vision, IMU, force/torque) and actuators (BLDC servo motors).
 Develop algorithms for motion planning, kinematics, and advanced control strategies.
 Collaborate closely with hardware and operations teams to ensure cohesive system integration.
 Create testing procedures for both simulation and real hardware to validate performance and reliability.
 What you will bring: 
 Proficiency in C++ or Rust (experience with ROS/ROS2 is a big plus).
 Strong foundation in control theory, kinematics, and dynamics of robotic systems.
 Proven track record of shipping code code for commercial or open-source robotics projects that have high impacts. 
 Experience with real-time embedded systems and safety-critical software.
 Excellent problem-solving skills and a willingness to adapt and learn.
 Hands on experience building and debugging electrical and mechanical systems.
 Knowledge of machine learning for robotics and advanced motion planning.
 Background using simulation tools like Gazebo, Mujuco or Nvidia Isaac Sim.
 Being able to speak Chinese and communicating with our vendors directly is a bonus.
 This role requires shifting working schedules and travelling to the US from time to time.

As the story goes, in 1949 Frank McNamara finished dinner at a New York restaurant and found he'd left his wallet in another suit. His fix was a card that let members eat now and pay later. That card became Diners Club, widely credited as the first multipurpose charge card. It was a piece of cardboard and a promise: the restaurant trusted the card, the card trusted the member, and someone had to make sure the money actually moved.
 More than seventy-five years later, the promise hasn't changed, but the machinery has. When a Mercury customer taps their card, the request goes from the merchant's terminal through an acquirer and a card network to us. In a fraction of a second, we check the balance, apply the customer's spend controls, screen for fraud and say yes or no. After that comes clearing, settlement, disputes and reporting, and every cent has to reconcile.
 Cards are the way Mercury customers spend money. The Cards Integration team owns the whole Mercury card, not just the swipe: issuance, physical card shipping, spend controls, lifecycle management, authorization, money movement, settlement and reporting, and the infrastructure underneath. We're a full-stack team, and our job is to make the Mercury Debit and IO cards reliable, correct, useful, and innovative.
 We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who thinks deeply about systems architecture, cares about the customer experience, and will dive into any problem to move the team forward. We value high ownership, working in pairs and teams rather than alone, and attention to detail. Those matter when you run systems held to four nines of reliability, and everyone around you will care about them too.
 In this role, you will 
 Lead projects from idea to tech spec to implementation to launch, working with your PM, EM, tech lead, and teammates at each stage. When you lead a project, it's yours to see through.
 Learn how debit and credit cards actually work under the hood (authorization, clearing, settlement, disputes) and use that knowledge every day.
 Build features across the stack, from the card experiences customers use to the backend systems that move money.
 Help keep our operations excellent. Our systems are some of the most observable at Mercury, and with great observability comes great responsibility.
 Mentor other engineers and raise engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, and collaboration.
 Work with product, design, operations, risk, compliance, sales, and many other teams.
 You should 
 Have strong full-stack experience, a product mindset, systems thinking, and a knack for getting things across the line.
 Have made architectural decisions on complex systems, and be able to explain your reasoning and the trade-offs.
 Be excited to put new features in customers' hands, and care just as much about keeping existing ones working like a charm.
 Care about correctness in systems where failure has real financial consequences.
 Communicate clearly, handle ambiguity well, and enjoy mentoring others.
 Be comfortable with our tech stack (Haskell and TypeScript) or be ready to learn.
 Bonus: experience in fintech, payments, or card issuing.
 We encourage you to try our demo site if you're interested in applying for the role.

 Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry.
